title: Interactive TokenFlow Playbook & Guided Stepper for Batching and Cache Recommendations
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers struggle to translate model-level batching/cache recommendations into safe, repeatable Console actions. Current recommendation cards are informative but lack a clear, low-friction path to preview, simulation, and safe rollout.

Goal: Design an interactive 'TokenFlow Playbook'—a guided stepper + simulator that surfaces tailored batching and KV cache recommendations, explains trade-offs in plain language, previews estimated token savings and latency impacts, and embeds guardrails (safety thresholds, prefix-safety checks, audit trail) so operators can confidently apply changes to Dedicated or Private environments.

Primary users: Platform engineers, ML engineers, and SREs managing inference cost/latency SLOs.

Out-of-scope: Deep kernel selection UI, runtime internals; those remain ENG surface. This is focused on the Console UX layer: recommendations, preview, simulation, and rollout controls.
design_notes: Introduce 'TokenFlow' branding as a lens within the model configuration page and the Recommendations hub to create a persistent mental model.
Stepper phases: Inspect -> Simulate -> Tune -> Guardrails -> Preview Rollout -> Apply/Plan. Each step collapses into a compact summary after completion.

Simulation: live slider for traffic mix and sequence length distribution; shows estimated throughput, median latency, p95 latency, and token-cost delta. Provide conservative/high-confidence bands derived from runtime profiling metadata.

Explainability: each recommendation line must include a one-sentence 'Why' and 'When to apply' microcopy, with a lightweight 'Show me the math' expandable showing assumptions (batch sizes, sequence-length percentiles, KV cache hit-rate assumption).

Guardrails: require explicit confirmation when recommendations touch 'prefill' or 'safety-sensitive' prefixes; display 'Potential behavioral impact' flag when cache changes could alter conversational history fidelity.
Audit & revert: every apply action creates a Console audit entry and a one-click rollback link; include a short rollback runbook in the success modal.
A/B experiment: variant A (inline stepper) vs variant B (modal guided wizard). Track completion rate, time-to-apply, and rollback frequency.
Accessibility: stepper must be keyboard-navigable and provide concise aria-live updates for simulation numbers.
Mobile: present a trimmed preview-only view for on-call mobile use-cases; full stepper reserved for desktop.
Integration hooks: add a 'Create PR' option for Private on-prem customers where changes can be exported as YAML to their infra repo.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity prototype implemented in Figma with interactive stepper states for all phases.
Engineering acceptance: ENG sign-off on data contract for simulation inputs (traffic mix, seq length dist, model profile) and guardrail signals.
Usability test: 6/8 participants (platform engineers) can complete the stepper and correctly interpret token-savings and risk indicators within 10 minutes.
Analytics: events instrumented for stepper open, simulate, tune, apply, rollback; experiment variant tagging present.
Security: audit log entry spec added to PM/ENG backlog for implementation; no PII is exposed in the preview modal.
Rollout plan: feature gated behind a console feature-flag and enabled for internal teams first.
Documentation: short 'How to use TokenFlow' doc in Console help center and a one-page runbook for customer success agents.
tasks: Design: create Figma prototype (desktop & trimmed mobile) and handoff tokens/components.
PM: finalize success metrics and A/B experiment design with Growth.
Eng: implement simulation API endpoint and agree on contract; add guardrail checks to recommendations API.
Eng: implement audit log entries and rollback endpoint.
Design: write microcopy for all guardrail confirmations and 'Show me the math' expanders.
QA: create test cases for simulation accuracy and rollback path.
Docs: draft Console help doc and one-page runbook.
decisions: Use a linear stepper (Inspect -> Simulate -> Tune -> Guardrails -> Preview Rollout -> Apply) to reduce cognitive load and provide clear checkpoints.
Simulation will use conservative/high bands; we do not show raw kernel metrics—only user-facing estimated impacts.
Automatic apply must be opt-in; default mode is 'Plan & Suggest' with an exportable YAML for Private deployments.
Prefix-sensitivity changes are surfaced with an explicit 'Behavioral impact' warning that blocks auto-apply until acknowledged.
Experiment to test modal vs inline stepper; telemetry will inform final placement in Console.
test_plan: Instrument Telemetry: stepper_open, simulate_run, tune_change, guardrail_ack, preview_rollout, apply_confirm, rollback_click; include experiment_variant.
Run 5 moderated usability sessions with platform engineers and 3 with CS agents using internal staging environment.
Bench test simulation API output against a blinded sample of production traces to validate estimated token-savings within +/-15%.
Smoke tests: apply then rollback in staging to ensure audit log integrity and rollback idempotency.
